activity.notes: Sayyida al-Hurra entered the political government of Tétouan after her marriage to Muhammad al-Manzari around 1510, becoming his principal confidant, deputy and eventually informal co-governor. Modern scholarship treats her pre-1519 authority as a co-ruling phase before she became the official sole governor after al-Manzari's death in 1519. ATLAS therefore records c.1510-1519 as a separate Co-regent Activity and keeps the existing 1519-1542 sole-governorship Activity distinct.

sources.title: Sayyida al-Ḥurra: An Early Modern Decolonial Muslim Exemplar — Religions
sources.citation_text: The peer-reviewed study states that Sayyida al-Hurra married the governor of Tétouan in 1510, became his main confidant, advisor and eventually informal co-governor, and officially became governor after his death in 1519.

sources.title: Gender and Authority: The Particularities of Female Rule in the Premodern Mediterranean — Arizona State University
sources.citation_text: The academic teaching text describes Sayyida al-Hurra as wielding authority in the Tétouan region from about 1510, initially co-ruling with her first husband and later governing alone.
